name: Congenital Anomaly of the Coronary Sinus

criteria.description: Identification of coronary sinus anomaly via echocardiography, cardiac MRI, or CT angiography
Absence or atresia of the coronary sinus ostium demonstrated on imaging
Presence of associated congenital heart defects such as persistent left superior vena cava or atrial septal defect

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of coronary sinus anomaly confirmed by imaging with at least one major criterion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily imaging-based; clinical presentation may be variable or asymptomatic.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent left superior vena cava draining into coronary sinus
searchTerms: persistent left superior vena cava draining heart vein
abnormal vein draining into coronary sinus

common.notes: Due to impaired coronary venous drainage
Arrhythmias secondary to anomalous venous return
Due to right-to-left shunting in associated defects

occasional.notes: Non-specific, related to altered coronary venous flow
Due to congestive heart failure in severe cases
Secondary to arrhythmias or low cardiac output

rare.notes: Due to paradoxical embolism via anomalous venous connections
Rare complication related to abnormal flow patterns

laboratory: Generally normal laboratory studies; no specific biomarkers identified
imaging: Echocardiography showing coronary sinus dilation or absence
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography demonstrating coronary sinus anomaly and associated vascular malformations
Contrast echocardiography revealing abnormal venous drainage
genetic: No specific genetic mutations identified; may be sporadic or associated with other congenital heart defects
other: Electrocardiogram may show arrhythmias or conduction abnormalities
Cardiac catheterization may confirm anomalous venous return

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of left superior vena cava draining into right atrium or left atrium without coronary sinus atresia
No absence of coronary sinus ostium
Acute presentation with chest pain and hemodynamic instability
History of trauma or invasive cardiac procedures

redFlags: Signs of congestive heart failure in infancy or childhood
Neurological deficits suggestive of paradoxical embolism
references: Anderson RH, et al. The congenital coronary sinus anomalies. Cardiol Young. 2010;20(3):243-252.
Goyal SK, et al. Persistent left superior vena cava: a case report and review of literature. Cardiovasc Ultrasound. 2008;6:50.
Ho SY, et al. Anatomy and pathology of the coronary sinus. Heart. 2004;90(9):1060-1066.
